source.extractionNote: All 4 variants read in full; intent from the Scrollbar Metadata frame, written 2026-11-07.

summary: The scroll indicator for a region that clips its content. A padded gutter holds a pill handle whose position and length mirror the scroll offset; hovering raises a track scrim so the grab target reads. Two orientations draw the same bar on either axis, and the scrolling region, not the bar, owns the behaviour.

intent.vertical: The axis the region scrolls. Vertical stands against the trailing edge of the content and the handle slides up and down.
intent.horizontal: Lies along the bottom edge for content that pans sideways, as the Table's frozen arrangement uses it.

state.note: Documentation-only in Figma; hover is a CSS state in code.

intent.default: The resting bar. The track is invisible and the handle sits quiet, so the bar reads as part of the content's edge rather than a control.
intent.hover: Pointer over the gutter. The track raises the ghost scrim and the handle darkens, which is what makes the grab target readable.

contentInputs.note: No Figma property. The handle's length is the viewport's share of the content (drawn at a sample 64Px) and its offset mirrors the scroll position.

anatomy.role: The component frame: a gutter holding the handle, padded space/2xs on every side so the handle floats clear of the content edge. It runs the full length of the scrolling region's edge.
A rectangle filling the bar behind the handle, interactive/ghost/background/default at rest and the hover token under the pointer — the same ghost scrim the buttons use.
The pill that shows the position: radius/pill, foreground/disabled at rest and foreground/secondary on hover. Its length is a sample of the value, not a property.

variants._note: Orientation and state are independent: the axes swap and nothing else. The @ opacities are Figma paint opacities over tokens that already carry their own alpha — see issues.

states.change: The handle draws in foreground/disabled over an invisible track. Only the colours are modelled; the handle's position and length come from the scrolling region.
The track raises interactive/ghost/background/hover and the handle moves to foreground/secondary. No pressed or dragging treatment exists.

behavior.description: Figma stores no timing and no transition is authored. Whether the bar fades in with scroll activity and out when it stops belongs to the implementation.
The handle's length is the viewport's share of the content and its offset mirrors the scroll position. The set draws one sample; nothing in it encodes a value.

content.description: Not a slot. A pill that takes its length from the value and its colour from the state; there is no property to restyle or hide it per instance.
Not a slot. The full-length gutter behind the handle, invisible at rest and scrimmed on hover.

do: Let the scrolling region own it. The bar reports position; wiring scroll, drag and keyboard belongs to the region that clips the content.
Match Orientation to the overflow axis — vertical beside a scrolling list, horizontal under the Table's frozen columns.
dont: Don't restyle the handle to look like a control. It has no focus state, so anything that invites clicking promises more than the set models.
Don't rely on hover to reveal the bar. A touch screen never hovers, so the resting handle has to be visible on its own.

accessibility: The set models no focus, pressed or dragging state, so keyboard scrolling and drag behaviour belong entirely to the implementation.
The resting handle is foreground/disabled on the page surface. Check it stays visible against the surfaces the region scrolls over.
Assistive technology reaches scrolling through the region, not the bar: expose the region and keep the bar presentational.
Hover is the only state change and colour its only signal, so nothing here reaches someone who cannot see the bar move.

layoutTheming.description: The gutter is 12 and the handle 4 as drawn, with neither bound to a token. The length runs the scrolling region's full edge.
space/2xs on all four sides, which is what centres the handle in the gutter and keeps it clear of the content edge.
radius/pill on the handle in every variant. The track has no radius of its own.
Drawn at a sample 64. In use the length is the viewport's share of the content and is never a property.
The handle is foreground/disabled at rest and foreground/secondary on hover. The track is interactive/ghost/background/default, rising to the hover token under the pointer.
vertical and horizontal swap the axes and nothing else: the same padding, colours and radius on both.

issues.detail: The gutter (12Px) and handle (4Px) thicknesses and the handle's sample length (64Px) are unbound — no dimension token anywhere on the set beyond the padding.

The track sets a paint opacity of 0 / 0.05 over interactive/ghost/background/*, which already carries the scrim in its own alpha — the same doubling Button has. Code binds the token alone with no paint opacity.

The resting handle binds foreground/disabled — a text-role token on a part that is not disabled. It resolves to the intended quiet grey, but a token meant for disabled text now controls scrollbar colour.
No pressed, dragging or focus state and no value are modelled, by design: the bar is the static indicator and the scrolling region owns the behaviour. Motion is not modelled.
Used by Table Content (frozen arrangement horizontal, vertical-scroll arrangement vertical) — see specs/table.
